source: Chinmay, in session, on the AI system design draft
rule: AI design questions are ours to answer; none was make-or-break, so none goes to the client

decisions.a: Yes; our own models per tenant
Managed Azure OpenAI re-billed per token; billing per selected module; 3 packages plus custom; module prices configured by TICVAI on the platform
UAE North for now; other regions configured tenant by tenant

All AI data retention is a TENANT configuration with a period per data class (prompts/responses, conversations, decision records, approvals). 90 days default for prompts; audit period is the default for decision records, not fixed. Law floors stay make-or-break. AI keeps metadata so it fetches from an index.
Start with minuted team; recommend second engineer if pace does not meet Block B
Knowledge from the vector store, live numbers from the semantic layer; numbers only from query results
Available; TICVAI decides per tenant whether to enable it
Model never works on data directly: scrub and bind figures, or the model writes code the platform runs
Raise to admin at threshold; never auto-switch
Every AI function inside the six months, baseline first (rules and starting patterns answer on day one), then it learns per tenant from that tenant's own data (Chinmay, 30 September)

Our proposal, adopted: each model carries a task-fitness band per agent task (AiModel.taskFitness: score, floor, ceiling, evaluation run); setAiProvider returns fitness warnings (underpowered, overpowered, unscored) and never blocks the choice
A second AI engineer from 5 October; no third (Chinmay, 30 September). The trained model producers slip first; everything with a baseline ships in the six months
